phases.name: Transaction ingress and online features
phases.description: Build a bounded synchronous decision path and obtain fresh behavioral features.

phases.name: Explainable risk scoring
phases.description: Combine versioned models, relationship signals, and online features into a reasoned decision.

phases.name: Learning feedback and reporting
phases.description: Move outcomes and graph/velocity updates asynchronously while preserving audit records.

phases.name: Operational evidence and thresholds
phases.description: Measure the stated targets and make model-quality tradeoffs observable.

steps.title: Separate the inline decision from learning
steps.content: The frozen brief requires real-time scoring, known and novel pattern detection, behavioral biometrics, graph-based rings, adaptation, low false positives, explainable outcomes, and compliance reports. It sets under-50ms scoring, 50k+ transactions/sec, false positives below 0.1%, detection above 95%, and explainability constraints. It does not define latency measurement boundaries, labels, fraud prevalence, review capacity, jurisdiction, retention, or model-quality evaluation windows. Keep feature reads and scoring on the synchronous path; graph updates, retraining, and reporting should not delay an inline transaction decision.

steps.title: Represent payment callers
steps.content: Merchants and payment clients submit transaction context and receive a decision plus stable reason codes. The fraud platform should not own the payment authorization state machine unless that boundary is explicitly part of the product.

component.label: Merchant & Payment Clients

properties.purpose: Submit transaction-scoring requests with an idempotency key and consume an allow, review, or decline recommendation with explainable reason codes.

component.highlightReason: The calling contract must carry enough context for scoring and return a usable decision without exposing internal model details.

steps.title: Scale the network entry
steps.content: Distribute stateless ingress across healthy instances and preserve a strict end-to-end latency budget. The 50k+ transactions/sec target needs capacity testing and does not by itself determine instance count or region topology.

component.label: Transaction Load Balancer

properties.purpose: Distribute scoring traffic across healthy gateway instances and expose overload signals for admission control.

component.highlightReason: A stable, horizontally scalable entry tier is necessary before the synchronous scoring path can be capacity-tested.

steps.title: Connect callers
steps.content: Use authenticated transport and idempotency to make client retries safe when a response is delayed or lost.

connection.label: Transaction score request
connection.description: The client submits a bounded transaction-scoring request over the public API.

steps.title: Add the scoring API
steps.content: Validate the transaction envelope, reject malformed or duplicate requests safely, and enforce a deadline that leaves time for online feature retrieval and model scoring.

component.label: Fraud Scoring API

properties.purpose: Validate transaction-scoring requests, enforce authentication and request limits, propagate deadlines, and return a decision with reason codes.

component.highlightReason: The measured score latency begins here only after the product defines the exact request/response timing boundary.

steps.title: Forward traffic to the API
steps.content: Keep the gateway in front of internal decision services so request deadlines, authentication context, and overload responses are consistent.

connection.label: Forward scoring calls
connection.description: Healthy gateway instances receive transaction requests from the load balancer.

steps.title: Authenticate the tenant
steps.content: Resolve the merchant or payment principal and its policy before feature access. A scoring result and its audit record must be attributable to a trusted caller.

component.label: Merchant Identity & Policy

properties.purpose: Authenticate merchant/payment principals, resolve tenant policy, and authorize access to scoring and reporting APIs.

component.highlightReason: Tenant identity scopes policy, audit attribution, and any customer-specific feature access.

steps.title: Connect identity to the entry path
steps.content: The API must authenticate before it reads profile features or returns a decision.

connection.label: Verify caller & scope
connection.description: The gateway resolves a trusted tenant and authorized scoring scope.

steps.title: Add a decision coordinator
steps.content: The coordinator owns the inline workflow: retrieve the required online features, invoke scoring under the remaining deadline, apply a calibrated policy, and return a decision. Keep third-party lookups and model training out of this path unless their latency is explicitly budgeted.

component.label: Transaction Decision Coordinator

properties.purpose: Orchestrate deadline-bounded feature retrieval and fraud scoring, apply a versioned decision policy, and return stable reason codes.

component.highlightReason: A clear synchronous owner makes the latency boundary, fallback behavior, and explainable decision contract testable.

steps.title: Pass verified transaction context
steps.content: Only trusted caller identity and validated transaction fields enter the coordinator; sanitize and minimize sensitive inputs before downstream processing.

connection.label: Authorized transaction context
connection.description: Verified tenant and request context enter the decision workflow.

steps.title: Add the online feature store
steps.content: Precompute and serve behavioral and transaction features with freshness metadata. Feature availability and fallback behavior need explicit definitions; do not silently treat missing biometrics as a low-risk value.

component.label: Online Behavioral & Transaction Features

properties.purpose: Serve low-latency, timestamped transaction, account, device, and behavioral-biometric features with explicit freshness and missing-value status.

component.highlightReason: Feature freshness and missingness are part of the decision evidence, not just implementation details.

steps.title: Retrieve online features
steps.content: Keep lookup keys bounded and batch related feature reads where the store supports it. The request deadline must include this dependency rather than measuring model execution alone.

connection.label: Fresh transaction features
connection.description: The coordinator requests time-bounded user, device, transaction, and behavioral features.

steps.title: State the missing measurement boundary
steps.content: The under-50ms constraint should be measured end to end across ingress, feature lookup, graph signal lookup, model scoring, and decision serialization. The brief does not specify percentile, warm/cold behavior, or dependency-failure policy; record these as validation questions instead of declaring an SLO met.

steps.title: Add the online scorer
steps.content: This service is the bounded inference endpoint and must fit within the brief’s under-50ms-per-transaction scoring target, including the timing boundary product owners define. It combines model outputs and returns calibrated scores plus stable feature/model reason codes; it should not make an opaque final payment action on its own.

component.label: Real-time Fraud Scoring Service

properties.purpose: Serve versioned fraud-risk inference under the under-50ms transaction scoring target and return calibrated scores, model version, and explainable reason codes.

component.highlightReason: Separating online model execution from policy preserves room for review/step-up outcomes and measurable latency.

steps.title: Invoke scoring with the online feature vector
steps.content: Send only the feature vector and transaction fields needed for the selected model, with freshness and missing-value markers preserved.

connection.label: Deadline-bounded score request
connection.description: The coordinator invokes the scorer with transaction context and retrieved online features.

steps.title: Represent known and emerging patterns
steps.content: Use a versioned ensemble that can combine supervised risk patterns with anomaly or novelty signals. A novel-pattern score is evidence for review and learning, not proof of fraud; validate it against labeled outcomes and false-positive impact.

component.label: Fraud & Novelty Model Ensemble

properties.purpose: Combine supervised transaction-risk models with novelty/anomaly signals and return calibrated risk contributions that can be inspected and evaluated.

component.highlightReason: Known-fraud classification and emerging-pattern detection have different evidence and calibration needs.

steps.title: Load an explicit model version
steps.content: Promote immutable artifacts with evaluation metadata and rollback provenance. Model updates should be staged and observable rather than changing in place during a transaction.

component.label: Fraud Model Registry

properties.purpose: Track immutable ensemble versions, training/evaluation metadata, approved status, and rollback lineage for online scoring.

component.highlightReason: Auditable version selection is required to explain which model produced a transaction decision.

steps.title: Bind scoring to a model artifact
steps.content: The serving endpoint records the exact version used so later reports can reproduce the decision lineage.

connection.label: Approved model version
connection.description: The scorer loads an approved, immutable model artifact and its calibration metadata.

steps.title: Add relationship analysis
steps.content: Represent relevant account, device, instrument, and merchant relationships as a graph or graph-derived feature source. Define edge provenance, access controls, and time windows; avoid turning weak association into an automatic adverse decision.

component.label: Fraud Relationship Graph

properties.purpose: Maintain time-aware links among accounts, devices, payment instruments, and merchants to derive candidate fraud-ring signals with provenance.

component.highlightReason: Graph relationships expose coordinated rings that isolated transaction features may miss.

steps.title: Supply graph signals to scoring
steps.content: Use bounded graph-derived features or a precomputed neighborhood view on the inline path. Avoid an unbounded multi-hop traversal that can consume the entire score latency budget.

connection.label: Bounded relationship signals
connection.description: Recent, provenance-bearing graph features are available to the scoring service.

steps.title: Supply behavioral and transaction features
steps.content: The scorer receives timestamped features so it can distinguish a genuinely low signal from stale or unavailable data.

connection.label: Fresh feature vector
connection.description: The online store supplies behavioral-biometric and transaction features with freshness metadata.

steps.title: Return scores and reasons
steps.content: The coordinator maps calibrated risk and reason codes into the caller’s decision contract. Thresholds must be selected against labeled data and business costs, not hard-coded from the brief.

connection.label: Risk score + reason codes
connection.description: Scoring returns model version, calibrated evidence, and interpretable reasons for policy evaluation.

steps.title: Explain the accuracy tradeoff
steps.content: Measure the false-positive target below 0.1% and detection target above 95% on the same representative, time-separated cohort with a declared fraud prevalence and label window, but report and gate each result independently; passing one does not compensate for failing the other. A threshold shift can improve recall while increasing legitimate-user friction; preserve review or step-up paths where the product supports them.

steps.title: Make the synchronous path the critical path
steps.content: The request path is ingress → identity → coordinator → fresh features and bounded graph signals → scorer → policy/reason codes → response. Keep event publishing, graph maintenance, model training, and report generation off this path. Define degradation behavior for unavailable features before claiming the latency constraint is met.

steps.title: Publish transaction outcomes asynchronously
steps.content: Capture decision, later confirmed outcome, and correction events without blocking the authorization response. Keep idempotency and event provenance so retries or reversals do not corrupt labels.

component.label: Fraud Outcome Event Stream

properties.purpose: Distribute transaction decisions, later fraud confirmations, reversals, and review outcomes to feature, graph, training, and audit consumers.

component.highlightReason: Asynchronous outcomes enable adaptation while protecting the transaction response budget.

steps.title: Emit outcome events after decision
steps.content: Publish a compact event after the synchronous response is committed. Do not include raw sensitive payloads by default; define retention and access policies for any fields that are necessary.

connection.label: Decision & outcome events
connection.description: The coordinator emits idempotent decision metadata and later outcome updates for asynchronous consumers.

steps.title: Add streaming feature maintenance
steps.content: Maintain velocity windows, device/account behavior aggregates, and graph edges from events. Use event time and late-arrival handling so out-of-order outcomes do not produce misleading features.

component.label: Velocity & Feature Stream Processor

properties.purpose: Update time-windowed velocity features and relationship signals from ordered/idempotent transaction and outcome events, handling late data explicitly.

component.highlightReason: Streaming updates improve freshness without adding asynchronous work to the transaction’s response path.

steps.title: Consume decision and label events
steps.content: Separate provisional transaction signals from confirmed outcomes; labels often arrive later and may be corrected.

connection.label: Ordered transaction outcomes
connection.description: The processor consumes decision and later-confirmed fraud events for derived features.

steps.title: Refresh online features
steps.content: Use idempotent writes and a consistent feature definition between training and serving to reduce training/serving skew.

connection.label: Updated behavioral features
connection.description: Streaming aggregates refresh online velocity and behavioral features for later transaction scoring.

steps.title: Refresh graph relationships
steps.content: Update edges from trusted, provenance-bearing events and support corrections or expirations when relationships are no longer valid.

connection.label: Time-aware graph updates
connection.description: The stream processor maintains graph relationships and derived ring signals asynchronously.

steps.title: Adapt models through evaluated training
steps.content: New patterns can enter a controlled retraining/evaluation loop. Prevent label leakage and use time-based holdouts. Treat the false-positive-below-0.1% target, fraud-detection-above-95% target, and explainability evaluation as separate promotion gates; record each result with its cohort and observation window, and require evidence before promotion rather than inferring success from the design. Compare false-positive/recall tradeoffs for legitimate users. The online-learning hint does not require unreviewed per-event weight updates.

component.label: Fraud Model Training & Evaluation

properties.purpose: Train and evaluate updated fraud and novelty models from confirmed outcomes using time-aware validation. Record false-positive-below-0.1%, detection-above-95%, and explainability results as separate gates, with cohort/window metadata and false-positive/recall analysis.

component.highlightReason: Controlled adaptation addresses changing tactics while protecting quality and compliance from noisy or delayed labels.

steps.title: Feed confirmed outcomes into evaluation
steps.content: Train on resolved labels and include the observation window in each dataset/model version; avoid using a model’s own unconfirmed decision as its ground truth.

connection.label: Confirmed labels & features
connection.description: Resolved outcomes feed offline training and time-aware evaluation.

steps.title: Register evaluated model versions
steps.content: Only candidates with separately recorded false-positive, detection, and explainability evaluation evidence become eligible for online serving; preserve the cohort/window and rollback evidence used for promotion. The architecture is not proof that any target has passed.

connection.label: Evaluated model candidate
connection.description: Training publishes candidate artifacts and distinct false-positive, detection, and explainability evaluation evidence to the versioned registry.

steps.title: Add a durable decision audit store
steps.content: Persist the decision, model version, relevant reason codes, policy version, and required provenance under strict access and retention controls. Avoid retaining full sensitive inputs unless explicitly justified.

component.label: Decision Audit Store

properties.purpose: Persist decision lineage, model/policy versions, reason codes, and required transaction references for investigations and regulatory reporting.

component.highlightReason: Explainability and compliance require durable, access-controlled evidence of how decisions were produced.

steps.title: Record decision lineage
steps.content: Write the minimal decision record reliably and make the write/failure semantics explicit; the product must decide whether scoring can return before audit persistence is confirmed.

connection.label: Decision & explanation record
connection.description: The coordinator records decision, model/policy version, reason codes, and transaction reference.

steps.title: Add compliance reporting
steps.content: Generate reports from governed audit records and resolved outcomes. Report definitions, jurisdictions, retention, and access roles are unspecified and must be confirmed with compliance owners.

component.label: Fraud Compliance Reporting

properties.purpose: Build access-controlled compliance and model-performance reports from governed decision lineage and resolved outcomes.

component.highlightReason: Regulatory reporting is a separate governed workload, not an inline scoring dependency.

steps.title: Build reports from audit evidence
steps.content: The reporting pipeline needs reproducible filters over policy/model version and outcome window; raw sensitive features should remain protected.

connection.label: Governed decision records
connection.description: Audited decision lineage feeds access-controlled compliance reporting and aggregate evaluation.

steps.title: Add model and service observability
steps.content: Track end-to-end scoring latency, sustained throughput, feature freshness, graph-signal availability, score distributions, reason-code frequency, false-positive and detection outcomes once labels mature, decision-level explanation coverage/fidelity, and model/policy versions. Keep latency, throughput, false-positive, detection, and explainability evidence separately attributable to its measurement window or cohort; do not combine them into one pass. Guard sensitive data in logs.

component.label: Fraud Decision Observability

properties.purpose: Observe scoring latency and sustained throughput, feature/graph freshness, model and policy versions, reason-code patterns, explanation coverage/fidelity, and delayed false-positive/detection outcomes as separate measures without logging sensitive payloads.

component.highlightReason: Each target needs independent evidence across live behavior and delayed, labeled outcomes.

steps.title: Load the approved ensemble for online scoring
steps.content: The model artifact and online serving endpoint are distinct catalog concepts: the serving component loads the approved ensemble and returns its version and explainable signals within the measured transaction budget.

connection.label: Versioned ensemble for inference
connection.description: The scoring service loads and executes the registered fraud/novelty ensemble.

steps.title: Measure model and feature behavior
steps.content: Monitor feature freshness, graph lookup behavior, score calibration, and delayed fraud labels by relevant population slices. Measure explanation completeness/coverage and fidelity/stability separately from latency and fraud-rate outcomes; preserve cohort/window metadata and investigate drift before model promotion. The brief sets no numeric explainability threshold, so agree its acceptance criterion with compliance owners rather than inventing one.

connection.label: Scoring & quality signals
connection.description: The scoring service reports model versions, latency, reason-code aggregates, calibration signals, and explanation-coverage/fidelity measurements.

steps.title: Measure stream freshness and capacity
steps.content: Use lag, event reordering, update failures, and partition skew to validate freshness and throughput rather than relying on aggregate broker capacity alone.

connection.label: Stream lag & feature freshness
connection.description: The processor exports throughput, lag, late-event, and graph/feature update health.

steps.title: Validate each target independently
steps.content: Run five independent validation gates and report each result separately; a pass on one does not compensate for another: (1) end-to-end scoring latency under-50ms, with timing boundary and percentile declared; (2) sustain 50k+ transactions per second at representative peak load; (3) false-positive rate below 0.1% on mature, representative labels; (4) fraud detection rate above 95% on the same evaluation cohort; and (5) explainability evidence covering decision-level explanation coverage, fidelity/stability, and model-version/reason-code traceability. The brief supplies no numeric explainability threshold or jurisdiction-specific regulatory threshold, so owners must define those criteria before judging this gate. The design alone cannot prove any target is met; do not report a pass before measurement.

steps.title: Close the unresolved product questions
steps.content: Confirm the inline decision contract (allow/review/decline), latency percentile and timing boundary, fraud-label maturity, acceptable review volume, fallback on missing features, model promotion criteria, report jurisdictions, and data retention. These choices materially affect architecture sizing and the trustworthiness of measured results.
